name: Terry Lin
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember trying to price a business that had once fed me.” Sunday often includes a stop at Harbour Bakery, where Terry buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I used to get invited to both houses. Once I put a price on the company neither was sure I could still come to dinner.
appearance: Terry has thick, tightly coiled hair, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a striped cotton shirt. It usually goes with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. When somebody else has the floor, Terry counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Terry always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Terry is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To get through a dinner where business can stay off the table.
family: Aldo Dixon is Terry’s stepsibling. Terry brings a spare shopping bag. Aldo chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The salon on strike*, Aldo says, “I quit my last salon over this and swore the next owner would hear my reasons before getting my notice.”
connections: Magdalena Macrae. They put the value of established customers beside the company's formal valuations.
